A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same logical-phase-transition and Neuro-Symbolic Curriculum Tuning study. All 24 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including Appendices A–F, support comparison; text, equations, tables, and figures are readable and matchable.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, model-specific phase-transition curves, curriculum ablations, and complexity analyses in the main text and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds comparisons involving further inference-time reasoning methods in Table 3.

M1.justification: The LoCM construction, NL–FOL model interpolation, supervised objective, and curriculum procedure in Sections 3.1–3.3 and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Evaluating the trained model with additional reasoning methods does not revise the proposed training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use ProntoQA, ProofWriter, FOLIO, ProverQA, and NSA-LR. The new comparison uses existing NSA-LR coverage and logical-complexity regimes, without adding a dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: New Table 3 evaluates ToT, DetermLR, and SymbCoT with and without NSCT on NSA-LR. Table 2 retains all original single-dataset tuning comparators and Naive/CoT comparisons; deleting Appendix B.4's explanations does not remove those evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Table 3 adds a paired comparison organized by reasoning strategy, reporting Low-, Medium-, and High-LoCM accuracy alongside overall accuracy. Existing splits, model configurations, training budgets, temperature-zero decoding, and Q4 evaluation remain unchanged. Strategy-specific settings for the added methods are not supplied.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds a check of whether NSCT gains persist across additional inference strategies and complexity bands. Existing component, interpolation, curriculum, operator, premise-count, and reasoning-effort analyses remain. The new FOLIO subsection interprets existing results rather than reporting a new error-analysis experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these comparisons. Existing correlation analyses are retained, and Table 3 continues reporting point accuracies without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports additional NSA-LR results, including overall accuracy without/with NSCT of 63.2/68.4 for ToT, 63.9/68.2 for DetermLR, and 64.8/69.5 for SymbCoT, plus complexity-band scores. These are newly reported comparisons; Table 2 and the existing appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The LoCM definition, critical-interval formulation, interpolation and loss equations, and Appendix D's formal syntax and translation rules are retained. No theorem, proof, derivation, or formal assumption is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about LoCM, logical phase transitions, and curriculum tuning. The headline average gains of +1.26 for Naive prompting and +3.95 for CoT are unchanged.

C2.justification: New Appendix C.4 interprets the existing FOLIO CoT decline as a possible mismatch between formal-logic tuning and commonsense grounding. Section 4.2 adds an interpretation of transfer across inference strategies, but incorrectly claims High-LoCM gains exceed Low-LoCM gains for CoT and ToT. The standalone limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds the HUST HPC computation-site acknowledgment and an LLM-use disclosure. Hardware specifications, hyperparameters, quantization, code/data access, and Appendix F prompts remain unchanged. The new statement that LLMs were used solely for writing conflicts with the retained GPT-5/Qwen3-Max dataset-translation account.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands the cited literature across the introduction and Appendix A, adding mathematical, multimodal, agent, and reinforcement-learning work, including AMO-Bench, DualVLA, and ARISE. Section 2 also explicitly distinguishes Shojaee et al.'s procedural puzzles from this study's propositional/FOL reasoning in complexity definition, evaluation target, and intervention scope.

P1.justification: v2 expands Section 4.2, condenses dataset descriptions, rewrites Appendix C.3, removes explanatory Appendix B.4, and adds acknowledgments and an LLM-use statement. The overall narrative structure remains intact. The new FOLIO discussion is referenced through an unresolved 'Appendix C.x' placeholder.

P2.justification: v2 adds the color-highlighted comparison table as Table 3, renumbers subsequent tables, and reflows surrounding text and appendix material. Existing figures, plotted content, and retained table structures remain unchanged; there is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added paired comparisons strengthen evidence that NSCT works with varied inference strategies, while acknowledging the FOLIO decline improves qualification of the findings. These are limited gains: new-method settings remain undocumented, the LLM-use disclosure is inconsistent, and Section 4.2 overstates High-LoCM gains—CoT gains +7.4 versus +8.5 at Low complexity, and ToT +6.1 versus +6.6. The core method and established results remain unchanged.
